mechanism_narrative: A one-week rebound in WORKPLACES from -16.1 to -6.6 indicates commuters returning to offices, which raises weekday foot traffic to retail and recreation venues and pushes RETAIL_REC above its last-28-day mean over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -16.1 at t-1w to -6.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is less than or equal to its last-28-day mean despite WORKPLACES rising by at least 5 points week-on-week at t-0w, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in PARKS below -15, observed at -16.7 in t-0w, signals that outdoor leisure is being suppressed by weather or restrictions, causing substitution toward indoor retail and recreation and lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-14-day mean falls below its last-14-day mean in periods when PARKS is below -15, the substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM stays above +5 and RESIDENTIAL stays above +10 simultaneously, households are localizing essential trips and staying home, which reduces discretionary retail and recreation visits and drives RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean exceeds its last-28-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM > 5 and RESIDENTIAL > 10, the localization mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Under a tightening-restrictions regime, TRANSIT below -17.5 indicates reduced permitted movement, which suppresses retail and recreation mobility and drives RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-14-day mean rises above its last-14-day mean when TRANSIT is below -17.5 under a tightening regime, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a normal spring reopening, PARKS should rise; the observed PARKS decline to -16.7 signals that seasonal outdoor demand is not materializing, and the same constraint keeps retail and recreation suppressed, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -13.4 at t-1w to -16.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is higher than its last-28-day mean while PARKS remains below -15, the seasonal-suppression hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility above +10 signals sustained work-from-home and local staying, which reduces trips to central retail and recreation districts and pushes RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean exceeds its last-28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL remains above +10, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A joint improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates returning commuters and transit riders, which raises retail and recreation footfall; when WORKPLACES > -8 and TRANSIT > -18, RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is lower than its last-28-day mean while WORKPLACES > -8 and TRANSIT > -18, the joint-commuting mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A stable GROCERY_PHARM level above +6 indicates continued essential-shopping priority, which crowds out discretionary retail spending and keeps RETAIL_REC below its last-28-day mean over the next one week.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-7-day mean rises above its last-7-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM remains above +6, the crowding-out hypothesis is rejected.
